Trace the same-lockbase nesting case the comment describes: mkdir fails because the outer lock holds it, the pidfile holds the parent's PID, bash does not change that value in a subshell so the liveness probe succeeds, and the loop spins fifty times and dies at :1090 reporting a state lock timeout held by the caller's own PID -- the single most confusing possible diagnostic for a self-deadlock, produced by the very failure the guard exists to name. The guard IS reachable for a case its comment does not describe, a locked body taking a lock on a DIFFERENT lockbase, which no locked body does today. Third, an undocumented platform asymmetry: the flock branch at :1012 never sets the depth, so on any host with flock the guard is inert for BOTH nesting shapes -- a cross-lockbase nested call is caught on macOS and silently permitted in CI, so CI structurally cannot catch the class the guard exists for. P2 because it is explicitly an internal assertion, but the documentation is the part that is wrong: the comment asserts coverage the guard structurally cannot reach. Fix: move the depth check above the until-mkdir loop so a self-deadlock is named as reentrancy instead of as a five-second contention timeout, set the depth around the flock branch's subshell too, and correct the comment to state which nesting shapes are actually detected. | 4 |  |

Findings demoted to Not Actionable by the False Alarm Filter. Future audits should NOT re-investigate them.
